about: paired-macs.sqlite3 as the first schema (user_version 1) wrote it: one table of Macs keyed by device id, with an upper-case UUID that v7 canonicalizes, and a Tailscale route that v8 turns into a migration grant. Seeded into a fresh paired-macs.sqlite3 (each `sql` statement, then PRAGMA user_version), opened through MobilePairedMacStore, and read with loadAll(): `macs` is what it must return, newest last_seen_at first. `newer_build_sql`, run on top, stands in for a build after this one (a new column, table and route kind): the same Macs must still read, and this build's next route write keeps the route it cannot read. Test: MobilePairedMacPersistedFormatTests (pairedMacStoreFixturesLoad).
sql: CREATE TABLE paired_macs (mac_device_id TEXT PRIMARY KEY NOT NULL, display_name TEXT, stack_user_id TEXT, created_at REAL NOT NULL, last_seen_at REAL NOT NULL, is_active INTEGER NOT NULL DEFAULT 0)

CREATE TABLE mac_routes (id INTEGER PRIMARY KEY AUTOINCREMENT, mac_device_id TEXT NOT NULL, route_id TEXT NOT NULL, kind TEXT NOT NULL, endpoint_json TEXT NOT NULL, priority INTEGER NOT NULL DEFAULT 0, FOREIGN KEY (mac_device_id) REFERENCES paired_macs(mac_device_id) ON DELETE CASCADE)
